title: Paid lines with CRM accounts
prompt: Revenue reporting wants every line of the paid invoices with the customer's name and country. Invoices and their lines are in the billing database; the accounts come from the CRM's nightly export, made by `crm_export`. Write `solve(invoices, invoice_lines, accounts)` so it returns `invoice_id`, `line_no`, `line_amount`, `account_name` and `country` for each of those lines.
rules: The starter saves the invoices and lines to the database and the accounts to the export. Read them from there.
Return one row per line of an invoice whose status is `paid`.
Keep a line even when its account isn't in the export; its `account_name` and `country` are then NULL.
A name or country missing from the export is NULL in the result, not the text `n/a`.
hints: Look at how `crm_export` writes the file. The read needs the same separator, header and missing-value marker.
The lines don't have an account: a subquery can join `invoice_lines` with `invoices` inside the database and keep only paid invoices.
Which join type keeps a line whose account isn't in the export?
explanation: Let the database do the first join and the filter: `spark.read.jdbc(url, "(SELECT l.invoice_id, l.line_no, l.line_amount, i.account_id FROM invoice_lines l JOIN invoices i ON l.invoice_id = i.invoice_id WHERE i.status = 'paid') AS paid_lines")`. Reading both tables and joining them in Spark works too. The export isn't a plain CSV file: `crm_export` writes `|` between values and `n/a` for a missing one, so read it with `spark.read.csv(crm_path, header=True, sep="|", nullValue="n/a", schema=accounts.schema)`. With the default comma each row is one long value, so no account matches; without `nullValue` a missing country comes back as the text `n/a`. Then `paid_lines.join(crm, on="account_id", how="left")` keeps a line whose account isn't in the export, which an inner join would drop.
starter:
def crm_export(accounts, path):
    # The CRM's nightly export of its accounts. Don't change it.
    accounts.write.mode("overwrite").csv(path, header=True, sep="|", nullValue="n/a")


def solve(invoices, invoice_lines, accounts):
    url = "jdbc:sqlite:/tmp/billing.db"
    invoices.coalesce(1).write.jdbc(url, "invoices", mode="overwrite")
    invoice_lines.coalesce(1).write.jdbc(url, "invoice_lines", mode="overwrite")
    crm_path = "/tmp/crm/accounts"
    crm_export(accounts, crm_path)
    # Read the lines of paid invoices from the database at `url` and the accounts from the CRM export
    # at `crm_path`, then return invoice_id, line_no, line_amount, account_name and country.
    return invoice_lines
